items.title: Abe Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: But those two are the main contractors and if you get a call from them, you’re in, if they start calling you. Well they stopped calling me a while back

ctx.x: Now this, you mentioned that he used a lot less people than the standard orchestra. Where is the status of the orchestra these days now in the film studios?

There are still, let me say it this way. In the union there are about, I used to think there was 10,000 but I think it’s about half, it’s about 5,000 let’s say. Of that there’s a group called RMA, Recording Musician’s Association, which I am not a member of ‘cause I don’t do that much work anymore. If I did I’d probably belong to it. Because those people, and there are only about, let me back up. The RMA has about 1,100 members within the union, Local 47, and that’s 1,100 out of 5,000, even 6,000. That’s a very…

way. And occasional calls. I have a call, I do some commercials and a few pictures, and once in a while, I don’t know what this one is coming up, I have something in a couple of weeks. In the meantime I do some jazz gigs or something. Luckily, busy enough.
